Alright, let me think through this year's plan. I'm 52, been farming this land for 35 years, and with senior high education I like to plan things out on paper before I commit. My farm is 18.4 mu total. Over the years I've settled on roughly 12 mu in cotton — that's my main cash crop and what Quzhou soil here grows best — and the remaining 6.4 mu in wheat-maize double cropping. The wheat-maize keeps us in flour and gives us some fodder and grain to sell if prices are decent. With just me and my wife at home and one of the kids working off-farm in Handan, we can't really handle more than that without hiring help.

**Cotton (12 mu).** It's late April now, so cotton planting is right on me. Soil temperature looks about right. I'll stick with the Lumianyan hybrid variety I used last year — it yielded 290 kg/mu lint on my west plot and the fiber quality held up at the gin. Seed runs around 45 yuan/mu. For nitrogen I'm targeting 15 kg N/mu total, split as 7 kg base in compound fertilizer (15-15-15) before bed-forming and 8 kg as urea at first flower. Phosphorus 5 kg P₂O₅/mu and potassium 7 kg K₂O/mu — cotton is a potassium-hungry crop and last season my bolls on the low end of the field aborted, which I think was a K issue. I'll plan 2 irrigations from the tube well: one right after sowing to get the seedlings up, and one at peak bloom in late July. If we get a dry spell in August I might add a third, but pumping costs 50-60 yuan/mu each time so I don't want to overdo it. Pesticide-wise, I'll do pre-emergence herbicide, then watch for aphids and bollworm — usually 2-3 insecticide sprays through the season. Cotton picking is the big labor cost — I'll hire village women for the three picks in September-October, probably 15-18 hired days at 80 yuan/day.

**Wheat (6.4 mu).** The wheat is already in the ground — planted early October last year. It's at stem elongation now, looking decent. I topdressed 10 kg N/mu as urea two weeks ago at jointing, which puts total N around 17 kg/mu counting the base I put down last fall. I'll irrigate once more at grain filling in mid-May if May stays dry. Harvest early-to-mid June with the combine harvester — I share the cost with two neighbors, works out to around 50 yuan/mu. Expecting around 480 kg/mu if the hot dry winds stay away in late May.

**Summer maize (6.4 mu).** Goes in right after wheat — usually June 15-18, can't waste a day because every lost day in June means lower yield at the other end. I'll no-till plant into the wheat stubble with the custom planter (hire the neighbor with the 2BYFSF-4 machine, 30 yuan/mu). Zhengdan 958 seed, that's what most folks around here run. One shot of base compound fertilizer at planting (about 25 kg of 15-15-15), then 10 kg urea topdress at V6-V8 stage. Herbicide once at 3-leaf stage. Maybe one irrigation at tasseling in early August if August is dry. Expecting around 520 kg/mu.

**Labor and cash.** I figure total input spend around 8,500 yuan this year, which is manageable — cotton will turn over that cash by October. Family labor is tight with just the two of us, so I'm budgeting about 25 hired days, mostly for cotton picking. My wife handles the wheat-maize plot mostly since it's less labor-intensive.
